artifact_design.artifact_type: Physics Unit Bank v2 design map
design_principles: secure families use fresh independent stimuli
no final prompt/choice/answer/solution prose at map stage

destination_notes.exit: 8-family section pool -> deterministic 4-family shared A/B/C blueprint
destination_notes.summative: 40-family Unit pool in two fixed 20-family blueprints; each form 16 SR + 4 CR and all 15 Unit I-cans

i_can_evidence_plan.i_can: I can explain why an object can be moving relative to one reference frame but not another.
i_can_evidence_plan.exact_i_can: I can explain why an object can be moving relative to one reference frame but not another.
i_can_evidence_plan.learning_target: Students will explain that motion is relative and describe an object’s motion using an appropriate frame of reference.
i_can_evidence_plan.evidence_job: Explain and justify how the same object can have different motion states when described from two explicitly defined reference frames.
i_can_evidence_plan.student_action: Compare the same object from two stated frames and justify why the motion descriptions differ without switching frames.
likely_misconceptions: reference frame can change mid-explanation without consequence
i_can_evidence_plan.notes_anchor_plan: Use one pair to model relative-motion reasoning and an additional pair to compare two frames because this is the section’s central conceptual dependency.
i_can_evidence_plan.practice_weighting_rationale: Weight strongly because students need repeated discrimination between frames and multiple viewpoint comparisons; use 11 of 30 families.
i_can_evidence_plan.secure_assessment_plan: Secure evidence should change observer/frame relationships and surface context while preserving the requirement to compare the same motion consistently.
formula_relationships: N/A — no formula is required for direct evidence.
formula_relationships_or_na: N/A — no formula is required for direct evidence.
tool_opportunities: student_constructed reference-frame sketch on blank response surface

i_can_evidence_plan.i_can: I can identify the reference frame used in a motion description.
i_can_evidence_plan.exact_i_can: I can identify the reference frame used in a motion description.
i_can_evidence_plan.learning_target: Students will explain that motion is relative and describe an object’s motion using an appropriate frame of reference.
i_can_evidence_plan.evidence_job: Identify the explicit or implied frame of reference that makes a motion statement meaningful.
i_can_evidence_plan.student_action: Determine which object/surface/observer serves as the frame and state the textual or representational cue that establishes it.
likely_misconceptions: assuming Earth is always the frame
confusing moving object with reference frame
i_can_evidence_plan.notes_anchor_plan: One direct Example/YTI pair is sufficient; focus on cue recognition before broader viewpoint comparison.
i_can_evidence_plan.practice_weighting_rationale: Use 8 of 30 families: enough retrieval and discrimination without crowding out the more demanding comparison I-cans.
i_can_evidence_plan.secure_assessment_plan: Secure items vary the described observer/object relationship and avoid relying on memorized labels.
formula_relationships: N/A — no formula is required.
formula_relationships_or_na: N/A — no formula is required.
tool_opportunities: student_constructed reference-frame sketch when construction supports explanation

i_can_evidence_plan.i_can: I can compare motion from two different points of view and explain why everyday motion is usually described relative to Earth’s surface.
i_can_evidence_plan.exact_i_can: I can compare motion from two different points of view and explain why everyday motion is usually described relative to Earth’s surface.
i_can_evidence_plan.learning_target: Students will explain that motion is relative and describe an object’s motion using an appropriate frame of reference.
i_can_evidence_plan.evidence_job: Compare two viewpoint-dependent motion descriptions and explain the practical convention of using Earth’s surface as the usual everyday reference.
i_can_evidence_plan.student_action: Reconcile two valid motion descriptions from different viewpoints and explain the Earth-surface convention.
likely_misconceptions: Earth frame is physically privileged rather than conventionally useful
i_can_evidence_plan.notes_anchor_plan: One complete pair should model reconciliation of two viewpoints; keep Earth-surface convention as reasoning, not memorized wording.
i_can_evidence_plan.practice_weighting_rationale: Use 11 of 30 families because this synthesis I-can integrates the section and benefits from varied viewpoint pairs.
i_can_evidence_plan.secure_assessment_plan: Secure variants must materially change the observer/frame configuration, not merely nouns, while preserving two-viewpoint reconciliation.
formula_relationships: N/A — no formula is required.
formula_relationships_or_na: N/A — no formula is required.

i_can_evidence_plan.i_can: I can calculate average speed from distance and time.
i_can_evidence_plan.exact_i_can: I can calculate average speed from distance and time.
i_can_evidence_plan.learning_target: Students will distinguish between speed and velocity and use distance, time, and direction to describe motion.
i_can_evidence_plan.evidence_job: Calculate average speed as total distance divided by total elapsed time and interpret the result with appropriate units.
i_can_evidence_plan.student_action: Extract or determine total distance and elapsed time from a physical situation or data representation, compute average speed, and report units.
likely_misconceptions: using one segment instead of total distance/total time
i_can_evidence_plan.notes_anchor_plan: Allocate two Example/YTI pairs: one direct contextual calculation and one representation-based or multi-segment average-speed route.
i_can_evidence_plan.practice_weighting_rationale: Use 13 of 30 families because average speed is the section’s main quantitative relationship and needs repeated direct, table, graph, and total-distance/time evidence.
i_can_evidence_plan.secure_assessment_plan: Secure families preserve average-speed evidence while changing data organization, physical situation, and relevant values; no exposed prompt reuse.
formula_relationships: v_avg = d_total / t_total
formula_relationships_or_na: v_avg = d_total / t_total
avoid_structures: inverse-only task that never calculates speed
tool_opportunities: graph_tool make_context_graph for supported position-time graphs
parallel_variation_axes: table vs graph vs prose givens

i_can_evidence_plan.i_can: I can distinguish instantaneous speed from average speed.
i_can_evidence_plan.exact_i_can: I can distinguish instantaneous speed from average speed.
i_can_evidence_plan.learning_target: Students will distinguish between speed and velocity and use distance, time, and direction to describe motion.
i_can_evidence_plan.evidence_job: Distinguish a momentary speed reading from a speed computed across an interval and justify the classification from the evidence provided.
i_can_evidence_plan.student_action: Classify speed information as instantaneous or average and explain which time interval or moment the evidence describes.
i_can_evidence_plan.notes_anchor_plan: One focused pair is enough; model the difference through evidence rather than pure definition memorization.
i_can_evidence_plan.practice_weighting_rationale: Use 7 of 30 families because this distinction needs repeated discrimination but less inventory than the quantitative and velocity-comparison I-cans.
i_can_evidence_plan.secure_assessment_plan: Change the evidence source (momentary reading, interval data, narrative) while preserving the classification demand.
formula_relationships: v_avg = d_total / t_total when average speed evidence is computed; no formula for a given instantaneous reading
formula_relationships_or_na: v_avg = d_total / t_total when average speed evidence is computed; no formula for a given instantaneous reading
avoid_structures: generic definition recall only across all items
tool_opportunities: semantic_html_table when interval data carries the evidence

i_can_evidence_plan.i_can: I can explain that velocity includes both speed and direction and compare examples of constant speed, constant velocity, and changing velocity.
i_can_evidence_plan.exact_i_can: I can explain that velocity includes both speed and direction and compare examples of constant speed, constant velocity, and changing velocity.
i_can_evidence_plan.learning_target: Students will distinguish between speed and velocity and use distance, time, and direction to describe motion.
i_can_evidence_plan.evidence_job: Explain why velocity requires magnitude and direction and classify/compare motion cases as constant speed, constant velocity, or changing velocity.
i_can_evidence_plan.student_action: Use speed-and-direction information to compare cases and explain when velocity changes even if speed does not.
i_can_evidence_plan.notes_anchor_plan: One pair should emphasize speed+direction and compare constant-speed/constant-velocity cases; YTI must change the direction pattern meaningfully.
i_can_evidence_plan.practice_weighting_rationale: Use 10 of 30 families because varied direction-change cases are needed to break the speed-equals-velocity misconception.
i_can_evidence_plan.secure_assessment_plan: Secure evidence changes direction histories and comparison structure, not just object names or numeric speeds.
formula_relationships: N/A for direct evidence; speed magnitude may be given numerically.
formula_relationships_or_na: N/A for direct evidence; speed magnitude may be given numerically.

i_can_evidence_plan.i_can: I can calculate acceleration from change in velocity and time.
i_can_evidence_plan.exact_i_can: I can calculate acceleration from change in velocity and time.
i_can_evidence_plan.learning_target: Students will explain acceleration as the rate at which velocity changes and identify acceleration from motion descriptions, data, and graphs.
i_can_evidence_plan.evidence_job: Calculate acceleration from a change in velocity over elapsed time, preserving sign/direction convention and units.
i_can_evidence_plan.student_action: Determine change in velocity from initial/final velocity evidence, divide by elapsed time, and interpret the acceleration with units.
likely_misconceptions: using final velocity instead of change in velocity
i_can_evidence_plan.notes_anchor_plan: Allocate two pairs: a direct Δv/t calculation and a representation-based acceleration calculation.
i_can_evidence_plan.practice_weighting_rationale: Use 12 of 30 families because acceleration calculation is a central quantitative pathway with multiple data and graph entry points.
i_can_evidence_plan.secure_assessment_plan: Secure families vary velocity evidence organization, sign patterns, and physical situation while preserving Δv/t reasoning.
formula_relationships: a = Δv / t = (v_f - v_i) / Δt
formula_relationships_or_na: a = Δv / t = (v_f - v_i) / Δt
avoid_structures: speed change with no direction/sign convention when direction matters
tool_opportunities: graph_tool make_context_graph for supported velocity-time graphs
parallel_variation_axes: table vs graph vs prose evidence

i_can_evidence_plan.i_can: I can explain that acceleration can involve speeding up, slowing down, or changing direction.
i_can_evidence_plan.exact_i_can: I can explain that acceleration can involve speeding up, slowing down, or changing direction.
i_can_evidence_plan.learning_target: Students will explain acceleration as the rate at which velocity changes and identify acceleration from motion descriptions, data, and graphs.
i_can_evidence_plan.evidence_job: Explain that any velocity change—magnitude, direction, or both—constitutes acceleration.
i_can_evidence_plan.student_action: Classify motion as accelerated or not from speed/direction changes and justify which part of velocity changes.
likely_misconceptions: constant speed with turning has zero acceleration
i_can_evidence_plan.notes_anchor_plan: One pair should contrast magnitude-change and direction-change cases so acceleration is not reduced to speeding up.
i_can_evidence_plan.practice_weighting_rationale: Use 8 of 30 families: enough varied qualitative cases to address misconception clusters without displacing graph/calculation evidence.
i_can_evidence_plan.secure_assessment_plan: Secure variants change how velocity changes (magnitude, direction, both) and require explanation of the changed component.
formula_relationships: N/A for direct evidence.
formula_relationships_or_na: N/A for direct evidence.
avoid_structures: acceleration formula substitution with no conceptual classification
tool_opportunities: student_constructed vector response surface when direction change carries evidence

i_can_evidence_plan.i_can: I can identify positive, negative, or zero acceleration from a motion situation and interpret simple motion graphs and connect them to velocity or acceleration.
i_can_evidence_plan.exact_i_can: I can identify positive, negative, or zero acceleration from a motion situation and interpret simple motion graphs and connect them to velocity or acceleration.
i_can_evidence_plan.learning_target: Students will explain acceleration as the rate at which velocity changes and identify acceleration from motion descriptions, data, and graphs.
i_can_evidence_plan.evidence_job: Determine acceleration sign/state from a motion situation or simple motion graph and connect graph behavior to velocity/acceleration meaning.
i_can_evidence_plan.student_action: Read a supported motion graph or motion description, identify positive/negative/zero acceleration, and explain the graph-to-motion connection.
likely_misconceptions: negative acceleration always means slowing down
i_can_evidence_plan.notes_anchor_plan: One pair must use an actual graph via graph_tool; YTI changes slope/sign behavior rather than merely values.
i_can_evidence_plan.practice_weighting_rationale: Use 10 of 30 families because graph/sign interpretation needs repeated representation work and misconception repair.
i_can_evidence_plan.secure_assessment_plan: Every secure direct sample uses an actual supported graph or equivalent data representation and changes graph parameters/sign structure.
formula_relationships: a = Δv/t may support graph interpretation but graph meaning is primary.
formula_relationships_or_na: a = Δv/t may support graph interpretation but graph meaning is primary.
avoid_structures: prose-only substitute for a graph-dependent evidence job

i_can_evidence_plan.i_can: I can explain why objects in free fall accelerate at the same rate when air resistance is ignored.
i_can_evidence_plan.exact_i_can: I can explain why objects in free fall accelerate at the same rate when air resistance is ignored.
i_can_evidence_plan.learning_target: Students will describe free fall as motion under the influence of gravity alone and use simple free-fall relationships to determine speed or distance fallen.
i_can_evidence_plan.evidence_job: Explain that ideal free-fall acceleration is the same for objects regardless of mass when gravity is the only significant influence.
i_can_evidence_plan.student_action: Evaluate or compare falling-object cases and justify equal gravitational acceleration under the no-air-resistance model.
likely_misconceptions: heavier objects fall faster in ideal free fall
any falling object is automatically ideal free fall
i_can_evidence_plan.notes_anchor_plan: One pair should explicitly confront the heavier-falls-faster misconception using ideal-model evidence.
i_can_evidence_plan.practice_weighting_rationale: Use 8 of 30 families because conceptual model discrimination is important but the section also requires substantial quantitative free-fall work.
i_can_evidence_plan.secure_assessment_plan: Change object properties and evidence format while holding the ideal model explicit; do not let context imply air resistance unless that is the contrast.
formula_relationships: g ≈ 10 m/s^2 as the shared ideal acceleration; no mass dependence.
formula_relationships_or_na: g ≈ 10 m/s^2 as the shared ideal acceleration; no mass dependence.
avoid_structures: mass-based calculation that implies different g
tool_opportunities: semantic_html_table when repeated-time evidence is provided
parallel_variation_axes: same vs different shape with air ignored

i_can_evidence_plan.i_can: I can use $g \approx 10\text{ m/s}^2$ to determine speed gained during free fall.
i_can_evidence_plan.exact_i_can: I can use $g \approx 10\text{ m/s}^2$ to determine speed gained during free fall.
i_can_evidence_plan.learning_target: Students will describe free fall as motion under the influence of gravity alone and use simple free-fall relationships to determine speed or distance fallen.
i_can_evidence_plan.evidence_job: Use the near-Earth free-fall acceleration model to determine speed gained over a stated time interval.
i_can_evidence_plan.student_action: Use v = gt for an object starting from rest in ideal free fall, compute speed gained, and report meaningful units.
likely_misconceptions: forgetting speed grows by about 10 m/s each second
i_can_evidence_plan.notes_anchor_plan: Allocate two pairs because this is the section’s primary direct quantitative relationship; include one representation-based pair.
i_can_evidence_plan.practice_weighting_rationale: Use 12 of 30 families for repeated contextual v=gt use across direct, table, graph, comparison, and error-diagnosis pathways.
i_can_evidence_plan.secure_assessment_plan: Secure families change time evidence, representation, and context while preserving ideal free-fall speed-gain reasoning.
formula_relationships: v = g t for speed gained from rest, with g ≈ 10 m/s^2
formula_relationships_or_na: v = g t for speed gained from rest, with g ≈ 10 m/s^2
avoid_structures: using a non-free-fall context without stating the ideal model
parallel_variation_axes: table vs graph vs prose evidence
speed gained vs compare two times

i_can_evidence_plan.i_can: I can use free-fall patterns to compare distance fallen during different time intervals and distinguish free fall from falling with significant air resistance.
i_can_evidence_plan.exact_i_can: I can use free-fall patterns to compare distance fallen during different time intervals and distinguish free fall from falling with significant air resistance.
i_can_evidence_plan.learning_target: Students will describe free fall as motion under the influence of gravity alone and use simple free-fall relationships to determine speed or distance fallen.
i_can_evidence_plan.evidence_job: Use the quadratic distance pattern of ideal free fall to compare intervals and distinguish ideal free fall from motion substantially affected by air resistance.
i_can_evidence_plan.student_action: Interpret or calculate distance patterns over time, compare intervals, and use deviations/conditions to distinguish ideal from air-resisted falling.
likely_misconceptions: equal distances each second in free fall
d = gt instead of one-half gt squared
i_can_evidence_plan.notes_anchor_plan: One pair should focus on time-distance pattern/interval comparison; keep air-resistance distinction explicit in YTI variation.
i_can_evidence_plan.practice_weighting_rationale: Use 10 of 30 families because students need both quadratic-pattern evidence and ideal/non-ideal discrimination.
i_can_evidence_plan.secure_assessment_plan: Secure variants change time intervals, data representation, and ideal/non-ideal evidence while preserving the same pattern reasoning.
formula_relationships: d = 1/2 g t^2 for ideal free fall from rest
formula_relationships_or_na: d = 1/2 g t^2 for ideal free fall from rest
avoid_structures: linear-distance pattern presented as ideal free fall
prose-only when a pattern table is the evidence

i_can_evidence_plan.i_can: I can represent velocity with arrows that show both speed and direction.
i_can_evidence_plan.exact_i_can: I can represent velocity with arrows that show both speed and direction.
i_can_evidence_plan.learning_target: Students will use velocity vectors, motion diagrams, and simple graphs to model and explain the motion of objects.
i_can_evidence_plan.evidence_job: Construct velocity arrows whose direction encodes motion direction and whose relative length encodes speed.
i_can_evidence_plan.student_action: Draw velocity vectors on an answer-neutral response surface using arrow direction and relative length to represent stated velocities.
likely_misconceptions: all velocity arrows can have equal length despite different speeds
arrow orientation represents position rather than velocity
i_can_evidence_plan.notes_anchor_plan: One complete pair must require actual vector construction; Example models the encoding and YTI changes magnitude/direction conditions.
i_can_evidence_plan.practice_weighting_rationale: Use 9 of 30 families with repeated construction/comparison paths because vector construction is an explicit representational target.
i_can_evidence_plan.secure_assessment_plan: Direct secure evidence uses a blank response surface and a fresh motion situation; no completed answer vector may appear in the student surface.
formula_relationships: N/A — vector magnitude may be numerical but direct evidence is representational.
formula_relationships_or_na: N/A — vector magnitude may be numerical but direct evidence is representational.
avoid_structures: selected-response recognition mislabeled as construction evidence
tool_opportunities: student_constructed velocity-vector blank HTML/CSS response surface
parallel_variation_axes: scale cue vs qualitative relative length

i_can_evidence_plan.i_can: I can compare velocity vectors to determine whether an object’s velocity is changing.
i_can_evidence_plan.exact_i_can: I can compare velocity vectors to determine whether an object’s velocity is changing.
i_can_evidence_plan.learning_target: Students will use velocity vectors, motion diagrams, and simple graphs to model and explain the motion of objects.
i_can_evidence_plan.evidence_job: Compare velocity vectors by magnitude and direction to determine whether velocity remains constant or changes.
i_can_evidence_plan.student_action: Construct or use answer-neutral vector evidence, compare magnitude/direction, and determine whether velocity changes.
likely_misconceptions: same speed means same velocity regardless of direction
different arrow location means different velocity
i_can_evidence_plan.notes_anchor_plan: One pair should compare two vectors after construction; YTI changes which vector component changes.
i_can_evidence_plan.practice_weighting_rationale: Use 8 of 30 families: enough varied vector-comparison cases while reserving more inventory for the multi-representation synthesis I-can.
i_can_evidence_plan.secure_assessment_plan: Secure families change magnitude/direction relationships and physical motion while preserving vector comparison; no completed answer vectors are supplied.
formula_relationships: N/A — vector comparison is primary evidence.
formula_relationships_or_na: N/A — vector comparison is primary evidence.
avoid_structures: selected response that claims construction evidence
tool_opportunities: student_constructed velocity-vector blank HTML/CSS response surface

i_can_evidence_plan.i_can: I can connect motion diagrams, data tables, and graphs to written descriptions of motion and critique an incorrect motion model and revise it using evidence.
i_can_evidence_plan.exact_i_can: I can connect motion diagrams, data tables, and graphs to written descriptions of motion and critique an incorrect motion model and revise it using evidence.
i_can_evidence_plan.learning_target: Students will use velocity vectors, motion diagrams, and simple graphs to model and explain the motion of objects.
i_can_evidence_plan.evidence_job: Translate among motion representations and written descriptions, diagnose inconsistency in a motion model, and revise the model using representation-based evidence.
i_can_evidence_plan.student_action: Use an actual graph/table or student-constructed motion diagram to connect representations, identify an inconsistency, and state or construct a corrected model.
likely_misconceptions: position, velocity, and acceleration graphs are interchangeable
model revision can ignore conflicting evidence
i_can_evidence_plan.notes_anchor_plan: Allocate two pairs because this is the section’s synthesis target: one graph/table translation pair and one model-critique/revision pair.
i_can_evidence_plan.practice_weighting_rationale: Use 13 of 30 families because multi-representation translation and critique need the broadest variety and feed secure assessment strongly.
i_can_evidence_plan.secure_assessment_plan: Secure families change the representation pairing, data/graph parameters, and inconsistency target while preserving multi-representation evidence; representations must be actual and answer-neutral.
formula_relationships: v=d/t or a=Δv/t may support translation when appropriate, but representation consistency is primary.
formula_relationships_or_na: v=d/t or a=Δv/t may support translation when appropriate, but representation consistency is primary.

sections.title: Speed and Velocity
sections.learning_target: Students will distinguish between speed and velocity and use distance, time, and direction to describe motion.

i_can_designs.i_can: I can calculate average speed from distance and time.
i_can_designs.exact_i_can: I can calculate average speed from distance and time.
i_can_designs.learning_target: Students will distinguish between speed and velocity and use distance, time, and direction to describe motion.
i_can_designs.evidence_job: Calculate average speed as total distance divided by total elapsed time and interpret the result with appropriate units.
i_can_designs.student_action: Extract or determine total distance and elapsed time from a physical situation or data representation, compute average speed, and report units.
likely_misconceptions: using one segment instead of total distance/total time
i_can_designs.notes_anchor_plan: Allocate two Example/YTI pairs: one direct contextual calculation and one representation-based or multi-segment average-speed route.
i_can_designs.practice_weighting_rationale: Use 13 of 30 families because average speed is the section’s main quantitative relationship and needs repeated direct, table, graph, and total-distance/time evidence.
i_can_designs.secure_assessment_plan: Secure families preserve average-speed evidence while changing data organization, physical situation, and relevant values; no exposed prompt reuse.
formula_relationships: v_avg = d_total / t_total
formula_relationships_or_na: v_avg = d_total / t_total
avoid_structures: inverse-only task that never calculates speed
tool_opportunities: graph_tool make_context_graph for supported position-time graphs
parallel_variation_axes: table vs graph vs prose givens

i_can_designs.i_can: I can distinguish instantaneous speed from average speed.
i_can_designs.exact_i_can: I can distinguish instantaneous speed from average speed.
i_can_designs.learning_target: Students will distinguish between speed and velocity and use distance, time, and direction to describe motion.
i_can_designs.evidence_job: Distinguish a momentary speed reading from a speed computed across an interval and justify the classification from the evidence provided.
i_can_designs.student_action: Classify speed information as instantaneous or average and explain which time interval or moment the evidence describes.
i_can_designs.notes_anchor_plan: One focused pair is enough; model the difference through evidence rather than pure definition memorization.
i_can_designs.practice_weighting_rationale: Use 7 of 30 families because this distinction needs repeated discrimination but less inventory than the quantitative and velocity-comparison I-cans.
i_can_designs.secure_assessment_plan: Change the evidence source (momentary reading, interval data, narrative) while preserving the classification demand.
formula_relationships: v_avg = d_total / t_total when average speed evidence is computed; no formula for a given instantaneous reading
formula_relationships_or_na: v_avg = d_total / t_total when average speed evidence is computed; no formula for a given instantaneous reading
avoid_structures: generic definition recall only across all items
tool_opportunities: semantic_html_table when interval data carries the evidence

i_can_designs.i_can: I can explain that velocity includes both speed and direction and compare examples of constant speed, constant velocity, and changing velocity.
i_can_designs.exact_i_can: I can explain that velocity includes both speed and direction and compare examples of constant speed, constant velocity, and changing velocity.
i_can_designs.learning_target: Students will distinguish between speed and velocity and use distance, time, and direction to describe motion.
i_can_designs.evidence_job: Explain why velocity requires magnitude and direction and classify/compare motion cases as constant speed, constant velocity, or changing velocity.
i_can_designs.student_action: Use speed-and-direction information to compare cases and explain when velocity changes even if speed does not.
i_can_designs.notes_anchor_plan: One pair should emphasize speed+direction and compare constant-speed/constant-velocity cases; YTI must change the direction pattern meaningfully.
i_can_designs.practice_weighting_rationale: Use 10 of 30 families because varied direction-change cases are needed to break the speed-equals-velocity misconception.
i_can_designs.secure_assessment_plan: Secure evidence changes direction histories and comparison structure, not just object names or numeric speeds.
formula_relationships: N/A for direct evidence; speed magnitude may be given numerically.
formula_relationships_or_na: N/A for direct evidence; speed magnitude may be given numerically.

sections.title: Acceleration
sections.learning_target: Students will explain acceleration as the rate at which velocity changes and identify acceleration from motion descriptions, data, and graphs.

i_can_designs.i_can: I can calculate acceleration from change in velocity and time.
i_can_designs.exact_i_can: I can calculate acceleration from change in velocity and time.
i_can_designs.learning_target: Students will explain acceleration as the rate at which velocity changes and identify acceleration from motion descriptions, data, and graphs.
i_can_designs.evidence_job: Calculate acceleration from a change in velocity over elapsed time, preserving sign/direction convention and units.
i_can_designs.student_action: Determine change in velocity from initial/final velocity evidence, divide by elapsed time, and interpret the acceleration with units.
likely_misconceptions: using final velocity instead of change in velocity
i_can_designs.notes_anchor_plan: Allocate two pairs: a direct Δv/t calculation and a representation-based acceleration calculation.
i_can_designs.practice_weighting_rationale: Use 12 of 30 families because acceleration calculation is a central quantitative pathway with multiple data and graph entry points.
i_can_designs.secure_assessment_plan: Secure families vary velocity evidence organization, sign patterns, and physical situation while preserving Δv/t reasoning.
formula_relationships: a = Δv / t = (v_f - v_i) / Δt
formula_relationships_or_na: a = Δv / t = (v_f - v_i) / Δt
avoid_structures: speed change with no direction/sign convention when direction matters
tool_opportunities: graph_tool make_context_graph for supported velocity-time graphs
parallel_variation_axes: table vs graph vs prose evidence

i_can_designs.i_can: I can explain that acceleration can involve speeding up, slowing down, or changing direction.
i_can_designs.exact_i_can: I can explain that acceleration can involve speeding up, slowing down, or changing direction.
i_can_designs.learning_target: Students will explain acceleration as the rate at which velocity changes and identify acceleration from motion descriptions, data, and graphs.
i_can_designs.evidence_job: Explain that any velocity change—magnitude, direction, or both—constitutes acceleration.
i_can_designs.student_action: Classify motion as accelerated or not from speed/direction changes and justify which part of velocity changes.
likely_misconceptions: constant speed with turning has zero acceleration
i_can_designs.notes_anchor_plan: One pair should contrast magnitude-change and direction-change cases so acceleration is not reduced to speeding up.
i_can_designs.practice_weighting_rationale: Use 8 of 30 families: enough varied qualitative cases to address misconception clusters without displacing graph/calculation evidence.
i_can_designs.secure_assessment_plan: Secure variants change how velocity changes (magnitude, direction, both) and require explanation of the changed component.
formula_relationships: N/A for direct evidence.
formula_relationships_or_na: N/A for direct evidence.
avoid_structures: acceleration formula substitution with no conceptual classification
tool_opportunities: student_constructed vector response surface when direction change carries evidence

i_can_designs.i_can: I can identify positive, negative, or zero acceleration from a motion situation and interpret simple motion graphs and connect them to velocity or acceleration.
i_can_designs.exact_i_can: I can identify positive, negative, or zero acceleration from a motion situation and interpret simple motion graphs and connect them to velocity or acceleration.
i_can_designs.learning_target: Students will explain acceleration as the rate at which velocity changes and identify acceleration from motion descriptions, data, and graphs.
i_can_designs.evidence_job: Determine acceleration sign/state from a motion situation or simple motion graph and connect graph behavior to velocity/acceleration meaning.
i_can_designs.student_action: Read a supported motion graph or motion description, identify positive/negative/zero acceleration, and explain the graph-to-motion connection.
likely_misconceptions: negative acceleration always means slowing down
i_can_designs.notes_anchor_plan: One pair must use an actual graph via graph_tool; YTI changes slope/sign behavior rather than merely values.
i_can_designs.practice_weighting_rationale: Use 10 of 30 families because graph/sign interpretation needs repeated representation work and misconception repair.
i_can_designs.secure_assessment_plan: Every secure direct sample uses an actual supported graph or equivalent data representation and changes graph parameters/sign structure.
formula_relationships: a = Δv/t may support graph interpretation but graph meaning is primary.
formula_relationships_or_na: a = Δv/t may support graph interpretation but graph meaning is primary.
avoid_structures: prose-only substitute for a graph-dependent evidence job

sections.title: Free Fall Motion
sections.learning_target: Students will describe free fall as motion under the influence of gravity alone and use simple free-fall relationships to determine speed or distance fallen.

i_can_designs.i_can: I can explain why objects in free fall accelerate at the same rate when air resistance is ignored.
i_can_designs.exact_i_can: I can explain why objects in free fall accelerate at the same rate when air resistance is ignored.
i_can_designs.learning_target: Students will describe free fall as motion under the influence of gravity alone and use simple free-fall relationships to determine speed or distance fallen.
i_can_designs.evidence_job: Explain that ideal free-fall acceleration is the same for objects regardless of mass when gravity is the only significant influence.
i_can_designs.student_action: Evaluate or compare falling-object cases and justify equal gravitational acceleration under the no-air-resistance model.
likely_misconceptions: heavier objects fall faster in ideal free fall
any falling object is automatically ideal free fall
i_can_designs.notes_anchor_plan: One pair should explicitly confront the heavier-falls-faster misconception using ideal-model evidence.
i_can_designs.practice_weighting_rationale: Use 8 of 30 families because conceptual model discrimination is important but the section also requires substantial quantitative free-fall work.
i_can_designs.secure_assessment_plan: Change object properties and evidence format while holding the ideal model explicit; do not let context imply air resistance unless that is the contrast.
formula_relationships: g ≈ 10 m/s^2 as the shared ideal acceleration; no mass dependence.
formula_relationships_or_na: g ≈ 10 m/s^2 as the shared ideal acceleration; no mass dependence.
avoid_structures: mass-based calculation that implies different g
tool_opportunities: semantic_html_table when repeated-time evidence is provided
parallel_variation_axes: same vs different shape with air ignored

i_can_designs.i_can: I can use $g \approx 10\text{ m/s}^2$ to determine speed gained during free fall.
i_can_designs.exact_i_can: I can use $g \approx 10\text{ m/s}^2$ to determine speed gained during free fall.
i_can_designs.learning_target: Students will describe free fall as motion under the influence of gravity alone and use simple free-fall relationships to determine speed or distance fallen.
i_can_designs.evidence_job: Use the near-Earth free-fall acceleration model to determine speed gained over a stated time interval.
i_can_designs.student_action: Use v = gt for an object starting from rest in ideal free fall, compute speed gained, and report meaningful units.
likely_misconceptions: forgetting speed grows by about 10 m/s each second
i_can_designs.notes_anchor_plan: Allocate two pairs because this is the section’s primary direct quantitative relationship; include one representation-based pair.
i_can_designs.practice_weighting_rationale: Use 12 of 30 families for repeated contextual v=gt use across direct, table, graph, comparison, and error-diagnosis pathways.
i_can_designs.secure_assessment_plan: Secure families change time evidence, representation, and context while preserving ideal free-fall speed-gain reasoning.
formula_relationships: v = g t for speed gained from rest, with g ≈ 10 m/s^2
formula_relationships_or_na: v = g t for speed gained from rest, with g ≈ 10 m/s^2
avoid_structures: using a non-free-fall context without stating the ideal model
parallel_variation_axes: table vs graph vs prose evidence
speed gained vs compare two times

i_can_designs.i_can: I can use free-fall patterns to compare distance fallen during different time intervals and distinguish free fall from falling with significant air resistance.
i_can_designs.exact_i_can: I can use free-fall patterns to compare distance fallen during different time intervals and distinguish free fall from falling with significant air resistance.
i_can_designs.learning_target: Students will describe free fall as motion under the influence of gravity alone and use simple free-fall relationships to determine speed or distance fallen.
i_can_designs.evidence_job: Use the quadratic distance pattern of ideal free fall to compare intervals and distinguish ideal free fall from motion substantially affected by air resistance.
i_can_designs.student_action: Interpret or calculate distance patterns over time, compare intervals, and use deviations/conditions to distinguish ideal from air-resisted falling.
likely_misconceptions: equal distances each second in free fall
d = gt instead of one-half gt squared
i_can_designs.notes_anchor_plan: One pair should focus on time-distance pattern/interval comparison; keep air-resistance distinction explicit in YTI variation.
i_can_designs.practice_weighting_rationale: Use 10 of 30 families because students need both quadratic-pattern evidence and ideal/non-ideal discrimination.
i_can_designs.secure_assessment_plan: Secure variants change time intervals, data representation, and ideal/non-ideal evidence while preserving the same pattern reasoning.
formula_relationships: d = 1/2 g t^2 for ideal free fall from rest
formula_relationships_or_na: d = 1/2 g t^2 for ideal free fall from rest
avoid_structures: linear-distance pattern presented as ideal free fall
prose-only when a pattern table is the evidence

sections.title: Velocity Vectors and Motion Modeling
sections.learning_target: Students will use velocity vectors, motion diagrams, and simple graphs to model and explain the motion of objects.

i_can_designs.i_can: I can represent velocity with arrows that show both speed and direction.
i_can_designs.exact_i_can: I can represent velocity with arrows that show both speed and direction.
i_can_designs.learning_target: Students will use velocity vectors, motion diagrams, and simple graphs to model and explain the motion of objects.
i_can_designs.evidence_job: Construct velocity arrows whose direction encodes motion direction and whose relative length encodes speed.
i_can_designs.student_action: Draw velocity vectors on an answer-neutral response surface using arrow direction and relative length to represent stated velocities.
likely_misconceptions: all velocity arrows can have equal length despite different speeds
arrow orientation represents position rather than velocity
i_can_designs.notes_anchor_plan: One complete pair must require actual vector construction; Example models the encoding and YTI changes magnitude/direction conditions.
i_can_designs.practice_weighting_rationale: Use 9 of 30 families with repeated construction/comparison paths because vector construction is an explicit representational target.
i_can_designs.secure_assessment_plan: Direct secure evidence uses a blank response surface and a fresh motion situation; no completed answer vector may appear in the student surface.
formula_relationships: N/A — vector magnitude may be numerical but direct evidence is representational.
formula_relationships_or_na: N/A — vector magnitude may be numerical but direct evidence is representational.
avoid_structures: selected-response recognition mislabeled as construction evidence
tool_opportunities: student_constructed velocity-vector blank HTML/CSS response surface
parallel_variation_axes: scale cue vs qualitative relative length

i_can_designs.i_can: I can compare velocity vectors to determine whether an object’s velocity is changing.
i_can_designs.exact_i_can: I can compare velocity vectors to determine whether an object’s velocity is changing.
i_can_designs.learning_target: Students will use velocity vectors, motion diagrams, and simple graphs to model and explain the motion of objects.
i_can_designs.evidence_job: Compare velocity vectors by magnitude and direction to determine whether velocity remains constant or changes.
i_can_designs.student_action: Construct or use answer-neutral vector evidence, compare magnitude/direction, and determine whether velocity changes.
likely_misconceptions: same speed means same velocity regardless of direction
different arrow location means different velocity
i_can_designs.notes_anchor_plan: One pair should compare two vectors after construction; YTI changes which vector component changes.
i_can_designs.practice_weighting_rationale: Use 8 of 30 families: enough varied vector-comparison cases while reserving more inventory for the multi-representation synthesis I-can.
i_can_designs.secure_assessment_plan: Secure families change magnitude/direction relationships and physical motion while preserving vector comparison; no completed answer vectors are supplied.
formula_relationships: N/A — vector comparison is primary evidence.
formula_relationships_or_na: N/A — vector comparison is primary evidence.
avoid_structures: selected response that claims construction evidence
tool_opportunities: student_constructed velocity-vector blank HTML/CSS response surface

i_can_designs.i_can: I can connect motion diagrams, data tables, and graphs to written descriptions of motion and critique an incorrect motion model and revise it using evidence.
i_can_designs.exact_i_can: I can connect motion diagrams, data tables, and graphs to written descriptions of motion and critique an incorrect motion model and revise it using evidence.
i_can_designs.learning_target: Students will use velocity vectors, motion diagrams, and simple graphs to model and explain the motion of objects.
i_can_designs.evidence_job: Translate among motion representations and written descriptions, diagnose inconsistency in a motion model, and revise the model using representation-based evidence.
i_can_designs.student_action: Use an actual graph/table or student-constructed motion diagram to connect representations, identify an inconsistency, and state or construct a corrected model.
likely_misconceptions: position, velocity, and acceleration graphs are interchangeable
model revision can ignore conflicting evidence
i_can_designs.notes_anchor_plan: Allocate two pairs because this is the section’s synthesis target: one graph/table translation pair and one model-critique/revision pair.
i_can_designs.practice_weighting_rationale: Use 13 of 30 families because multi-representation translation and critique need the broadest variety and feed secure assessment strongly.
i_can_designs.secure_assessment_plan: Secure families change the representation pairing, data/graph parameters, and inconsistency target while preserving multi-representation evidence; representations must be actual and answer-neutral.
formula_relationships: v=d/t or a=Δv/t may support translation when appropriate, but representation consistency is primary.
formula_relationships_or_na: v=d/t or a=Δv/t may support translation when appropriate, but representation consistency is primary.

planned_slots.student_action: Use the shared stimulus across connected labeled parts, identify what each part needs, and explicitly carry an earlier result/interpretation into a later part.

planned_slots.authoring_notes: Design one coherent WTC around shared free-fall time-speed table whose earlier pattern inference supports a later prediction. Underlying Physics should remain structurally accessible; the navigation/decomposition work is the purpose. Do not author a loose preview list.
planned_slots.wording_length_intent: One coherent 3-5 part FRQ routine; concise part wording around one shared stimulus.
